name: Site footer
explanation: The area at the bottom of every page with links such as contact, privacy policy, terms and social media.
triggers: footer;add a footer;links at the bottom;copyright notice;copyright year;privacy and terms links
requirements: Use the footer element so it becomes the contentinfo landmark;Include contact, privacy, terms and accessibility statement links where needed;Group links under short headings;Update the copyright year automatically;Use descriptive link text with readable contrast;Stack columns into one on small screens
done_when: Screen reader users can jump to the footer by landmark;Every footer link works and has a clear name;The footer stays readable on a phone

name: Hero section
explanation: The large banner at the top of a landing page, with a main headline, a short message, a call-to-action button and often a big image.
synonyms: hero banner;jumbotron;hero image;above the fold;landing page header
triggers: landing page;big headline;big image at the top;headline at the top;top of the landing page;main banner;big banner;first thing visitors see
requirements: Use one h1 for the main headline;Make the call to action a real link or button with clear text;Keep text over an image at 4.5:1 contrast, adding an overlay if needed;Load the hero image early with fetchpriority=high, since it is often the Largest Contentful Paint;Give the image a width and height or aspect ratio so nothing shifts;Avoid autoplaying video, or add a pause control and respect reduced motion;Serve smaller images to phones with srcset
done_when: The headline and button are readable on every screen size;The hero loads fast enough to keep LCP under 2.5 seconds;Nothing moves or shifts after the page loads

name: Table of contents
explanation: A list of links to the sections of a long page, often kept in a sidebar and highlighting the section being read.
synonyms: in-page navigation;on this page;scrollspy;jump links;anchor links
triggers: links to sections;jump to section;highlight current section;long article navigation;sections on this page;contents list
requirements: Use a nav element labelled On this page;Give headings stable ids so links keep working when the text changes;Highlight the current section while scrolling and mark it with aria-current;Use scroll-margin-top so a sticky header does not cover the target heading;Scroll smoothly only when the user does not prefer reduced motion;Keep it in a sticky sidebar on wide screens and collapsible on phones
done_when: Each link jumps to its section without hiding it under the header;The current section is highlighted while scrolling;Links to a section can be shared and open in the right place

name: Announcement banner
explanation: A strip at the top of every page with an important sitewide message, such as planned downtime or a policy change.
synonyms: site-wide banner;announcement bar;site alert;notice bar;top banner
triggers: message at the top of every page;banner at the top;maintenance notice;scheduled downtime message;sitewide message;dismiss the banner
requirements: Keep it short, with one clear link to details;Let users dismiss it, and remember that for this message only;Do not use role=alert for a message that is already there when the page loads;Show it in the same place on every page;Reserve its height so it does not push content down after loading;Give each message start and end times so old ones disappear;Keep it for important news rather than marketing
done_when: A dismissed message stays hidden on later visits;The page does not jump when the banner appears;Expired messages stop showing on time

name: Check your answers page
explanation: A page at the end of a form that lists all the user's answers so they can review and change them before submitting.
synonyms: review page;summary page;review before submit;order review
triggers: review before submitting;summary before submit;check before sending;check my answers;all their answers;before they submit;change an answer;confirm details before
requirements: Show every question and answer, grouped by section;Give each answer a Change link that goes to the question and then back to this page;Add visually hidden text to change links, such as Change name;Put any declaration and the final submit button at the bottom;Prevent a double click from submitting twice;Mark up the answers as a summary list, such as a description list
done_when: Users can change any answer and come straight back;Screen readers announce which answer each Change link edits;Clicking submit twice sends only one application

name: Task list page
explanation: A page listing the parts of a long application or setup, showing which are done, so users can complete them in any order.
synonyms: task list;setup checklist;onboarding checklist;getting started checklist
triggers: in any order;setup steps;complete sections in any order;steps to finish setup;profile completion;sections to complete;what is left to do;setup progress
requirements: Show each task with a clear status, such as Not started, In progress or Completed;Let users complete tasks in any order unless one depends on another;Show overall progress, such as 3 of 5 completed;Mark tasks that cannot start yet, and say why;Save progress so users can leave and come back;Make each task name a link and show the status as text, not colour alone
done_when: Users see what is left to do at a glance;Progress is kept when users sign out and come back;Statuses are clear without colour

name: Confirmation page
explanation: The page shown after a form, order or payment succeeds, confirming it worked and saying what happens next.
synonyms: success page;thank you page;order confirmation;receipt page
triggers: after submitting;thank you message;order complete;reference number;what happens next;payment successful page
requirements: Use a clear heading, such as Application complete or Order placed;Show a reference number that users can copy;Explain what happens next and when;Send the same details by email;Make sure refreshing the page or going back does not submit again;Link to the next useful task or a short feedback survey
done_when: Refreshing the page never creates a duplicate order;Users get the reference number on screen and by email;Users know what will happen next

name: 404 page
explanation: The page shown when an address does not exist, helping the user find what they were looking for.
triggers: page does not exist;broken link;wrong url;missing page;dead link;404 error
requirements: Return a real 404 status code, not 200;Use a plain heading such as Page not found;Suggest checking the address, and link to the home page or search;Keep the normal site header and navigation;Log 404s so broken links can be fixed or redirected;Redirect moved pages with a 301 instead of showing a 404
done_when: Missing pages return status 404 and are not indexed;Users can continue to useful content from the page;Frequent broken links show up in the logs

name: Error and maintenance pages
explanation: The page shown when the site is down for maintenance or has a server error, explaining what happened and when it will be back.
synonyms: maintenance page;500 error page;503 page;error page;downtime page
triggers: site is down;down for maintenance;server error page;temporarily unavailable;outage page;sorry there is a problem
requirements: Return 503 for planned maintenance and 500 for unexpected errors;Add a Retry-After header when you know when the service will be back;Tell users when the service will be back, if you know;Say what users can do meanwhile, such as other ways to get help;Never show stack traces or technical details to users;Serve the page as a static file or from a CDN so it works when the app is down
done_when: During maintenance, users and search engines get a 503 with a clear message;Error pages never reveal internal details;The page still loads when the application server is down

name: Quick exit button
explanation: A button that instantly leaves a sensitive website, such as a domestic abuse support site, by going to a neutral page.
synonyms: exit this page;safety exit;panic button;leave this site quickly
triggers: hide the site quickly;leave the site fast;escape button for victims;domestic abuse website;close the site in a hurry
requirements: Show the button in the same place on every page and keep it visible while scrolling;Send users to a neutral site, such as a weather or search page;Open the neutral site in the same tab and replace the current history entry;Offer a keyboard shortcut, such as pressing Shift three times, and explain it;Explain that it does not clear browsing history, and link to safety advice;Avoid storing anything on the device that reveals the visit, where possible
done_when: One click or tap leaves the site immediately;The back button does not return to the page the user was on;The keyboard shortcut works on every page
